entry.title: .Neemad: Mohammad Ghouchani, journalist and political figure, recently in a…
entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

.Neemad: Mohammad Ghouchani, journalist and political figure, recently in a note titled "Masked Liberalism" claimed the end of the "religious intellectualism" movement, and through this, targeted Abdolkarim Soroush, the philosopher and one of the main figures of this intellectual current in Iran. In this note, he accused Mr. Soroush of "purging the university" and wrote that "he has succumbed to the wave of neo-Marxism" and that Soroush "speaks in the language of the left and explains the competitive free market system with the label of capitalism." Soroush Dabbagh, philosopher and psychologist, who himself is among the religious modernists, has responded to Mr. Ghouchani in this note published by Neemad. Neemad welcomes discussion on this matter. *** "Reference. To write honestly, given the turbulent and worrying situation of the country and in the midst of ceasefire, war, executions, runaway inflation, the fuel crisis... I preferred, as a member of the intellectual family, not to enter further into the dust that has recently appeared in the atmosphere, and to suffice with the two writings 'A Suitcase of Lies' and 'Shariati, Chandelle, and Being Muslim'. But the publication of the writing 'Masked Liberalism' led me to write the following lines. May it be of use to discerning audiences and those who monitor the intellectual developments of contemporary Iran. A few months after the controversial and contentious presidential election of June 2009, around the publication of the first issue of the new religious modernists, he has also severely criticized and attacked the leftist intellectual tradition from the perspective of liberal teachings and the free market economy.[1] Although I was not and am not in agreement with his attitude and method of analysis and arguments; nonetheless, I did not fault him for this, because theoretical-political housecleaning and revisionism is the right of any researcher, writer, and journalist. But, upon reading his recent writing, I realized that the story goes beyond this and has clear non-epistemic dimensions. It is of the nature of ethnic-tribal confrontation, mixing oil and water, labeling, and building files; that 'whoever is not killed is not of our tribe'. To justify my claim, I will address several clear errors and mistakes in the writing 'Masked Liberalism' and pass over the rest, as per the example: 'The rest of this poem, O noble minstrel, count in this manner, for this manner is my desire'..." entry.title: This Saturday, I gave a lecture titled "The Guardian of Language and the World:…
entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

This Saturday, I gave a lecture titled "The Guardian of Language and the World: The Relation of Language, Meaning, and Life in the Early Wittgenstein" at the "Science and Theology" Center, at the Institute for Fundamental Studies of Beheshti University, among philosophy students and philosophy researchers. The audio file of this session has been posted on my Telegram channel, and interested audiences can download and listen to it. The discussion and dialogue with philosophy researchers who are seriously engaged in philosophical study, work, and practice within the country was, in its own right, a valuable, soul-refreshing, and memorable experience for me, even though it was conducted remotely and virtually. Those interested can read a report of this session, which was published in one of the journals, through the image above. https://www.instagram.com/p/DcMqtAjR1Y1/?igsi=MXZvYzB2NWg0N3JscA==

entry.title: Whisper 9. "The solution to the problem of life can be seen in the…
entry.summary:
Source: @Soroushdabbagh_Official

Whisper 9. "The solution to the problem of life can be seen in the disappearance of this problem. Is this not the reason why those who, after a long period of doubt, have come to see the meaning of life, have been unable to say what this meaning is? Indeed, there are things that cannot be put into words. They show themselves. They are the mystical." The above passages belong to the groundbreaking work "Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus"; a time when Wittgenstein was fighting in the Austrian army and simultaneously working on the final version of the book, carrying it in his backpack. Undoubtedly, facing death on the front lines had a profound impact on the writing of the final passages of the "Tractatus Logico-Philosophicus," passages that carry strong existential undertones and are deeply intertwined with the being of the young Ludwig. There is no escape from addressing the "meaning of life," for man is a meaning-seeking and meaning-finding animal. A pure insight ripples through Wittgenstein's account of the meaning of life; a fluidity and elusiveness can be seen in it; one can neither ignore it, forget it, nor abandon it, nor can one formulate it neatly and do it justice in language, with the help of words, propositions, and phrases. As Rumi whispered to himself in the "Divan-e Shams": "Catch the hem of His grace, for He may suddenly flee / But do not pull Him like an arrow, for He may escape from the bow." Wittgenstein's tone and manner of phrasing in the above passages evoke the tone and phrases of the "Holy Bible." It is as if, as Jung and Kazantzakis have noted, the young Ludwig is the second creator of the world, seeking to complete the half-finished work of creation. In fact, he has given meaning to his life by producing original creative works and depositing an elixir within them; just as Forough and Sohrab did by creating the poems "Earthly Verses" and "Surah of Watching" in the collections "Another Birth" and "The Green Volume." Quoted from: "Velvet Whispers: Existential Murmurs," Volume Two, Author: Soroush Dabbagh. https://www.instagram.com/p/DcG8fivRzLW/?igsh=MXBzNW56N2Zseml3bg==
